title: Review assessment
description: Body of an 'assessment' artifact: an independent review's verdict and findings, bound to the exact subject it reviewed (REQ-TEAM-5, REQ-WF-5). 1.1 (ADR-0075): findings are important, nit, or pre-existing, with their evidence, class, and a second reviewer's vote; the verdict is changes-requested only while a confirmed important finding stands; a summary opens with the count.

subject.description: The exact subject reviewed; it equals the subject current when the review was accepted.

verdict.description: 1.1: changes-requested only while a confirmed important finding stands; never for one still waiting for its verification, nor for nits or pre-existing findings alone.

said.description: 1.1: the verdict the reviewer wrote, when the engine's reading of the severities changed it.

summary.description: 1.1: the review in a sentence, opening with the count of its findings by severity ('2 important, 3 nits', or 'no issues').

approach.description: 1.1: from review cycle 3 on, whether the reviewer thinks the approach should change rather than be fixed again, and why.

id.description: 1.1: the finding's id within its review (f1, f2, ...), what a vote and an author's response name.

severity.description: 1.1 writes important (a real defect of this change), nit (style, naming, wording, a small improvement), or pre-existing (a defect the change did not introduce); 1.0 wrote blocking, warning, info.

line.description: 1.1: the line of the file the evidence points at.

evidence.description: 1.1: what fails, and how the file and line show it. An important or pre-existing finding without a file, a line, and evidence is read as a nit.

class.description: 1.1: the class of defect, so the author fixes every instance of it.

demoted.description: 1.1: the reviewer said important or pre-existing with no file, line, or evidence, so the finding is read as a nit.

repeated.description: 1.1: the earlier finding (review step#id) already answered that this one repeats; it is shown, never counted or sent.

verification.description: 1.1: a second reviewer's vote on an important finding; only confirm makes it block. none: it gave no vote, so the finding stays unverified and does not block.
